report.summary: Analyzed transport.py chunk; found one broken claim (CompositeTransportSink failure isolation) and two observations.
risks: line 42-44 | medium | CompositeTransportSink does not handle exceptions from individual sinks; a failing sink will prevent subsequent sinks from receiving the record. | Add try-except around each sink.publish to isolate failures.

handoff.purpose: Defines transport sink protocol and implementations for runtime shell records.

symbols.name: CompositeTransportSink
symbols.note: Fans out records to multiple sinks.

claims.text: Persist or forward one lossless transport record.
claims.why: The docstring describes a contract, but the protocol stub does not implement persistence or forwarding; implementations may vary.

claims.text: Small deterministic sink for tests and embedded consumers.
claims.why: The class stores records in a list, which is deterministic and suitable for tests.

claims.text: Append-only JSONL journal preserving every normalized input/output.
claims.why: The publish method opens the file in append mode and writes a JSON line per record.

claims.text: Fan one record out to multiple sinks; failures remain visible.
claims.why: The publish method iterates over sinks and awaits each, but does not catch exceptions; failures will propagate and stop subsequent sinks, making failures visible but not isolating them.

observations.what: CompositeTransportSink does not handle exceptions from individual sinks; a failing sink will prevent subsequent sinks from receiving the record.
JsonlTransportSink uses asyncio.Lock but the file write is synchronous; the lock only prevents interleaving of async tasks, not inter-process or inter-thread writes.
